questions.q: A patient with severe protein malnutrition in Maiduguri develops swollen legs. Which change in blood plasma most directly explains the swelling?
options: A rise in capillary blood pressure causes more tissue fluid to return to the blood.
An increase in capillary permeability allows plasma protein to leak into tissue fluid.
A fall in plasma protein concentration reduces the osmotic return of tissue fluid into capillaries.
An increase in plasma protein concentration draws water from tissue fluid into capillaries.
questions.explanation: Severe protein malnutrition lowers plasma protein concentration, so the osmotic pull drawing tissue fluid back into capillaries is reduced; fluid accumulates in tissues and causes swelling. Increasing plasma protein would draw more water back into the blood, which would reduce rather than cause oedema.

questions.q: A farmer in Jos removes a complete ring of bark from the stem of a citrus tree. The roots may eventually die mainly because
options: sugar made in the leaves cannot reach the roots through the phloem.
carbon dioxide cannot diffuse into the leaves through the lenticels.
water absorbed by the roots cannot reach the leaves through the xylem.
mineral salts in the bark cannot be transported to the leaves.
questions.explanation: Ring-barking removes the phloem, which carries sugars made in the leaves to the roots. Without sugars for respiration, root cells eventually die, even though xylem water transport may continue for some time.

questions.q: During a suspected outbreak of typhoid fever in a school in Ogbomoso, which measure most directly interrupts the faecal–oral route of transmission?
options: Giving vitamin A supplements to every pupil
Providing safe drinking water and safe disposal of sewage
Isolating all pupils with fever for one week
questions.explanation: Typhoid fever spreads mainly by food or water contaminated with faeces, so safe water and safe sewage disposal directly block this route. Killing mosquitoes targets malaria, while vitamin A or isolating fever cases does not directly stop faecal–oral contamination.

questions.q: A patient in Ibadan is diagnosed with tuberculosis and is placed on a combination of antibiotics for several months. Why is combination therapy important?
options: It removes the need for good nutrition and rest.
It prevents the patient from catching malaria during treatment.
It reduces the chance of the bacteria developing resistance to a single drug.
It makes the antibiotics effective against viruses.
questions.explanation: Tuberculosis is treated with several antibiotics together because a combination reduces the chance that resistant bacteria survive and multiply. Using one drug for too short a time allows resistant strains to be selected.

questions.q: A driver in Lagos sees a red traffic light and voluntarily presses the brake. Which part of the brain is mainly responsible for interpreting the visual signal and initiating this voluntary action?
questions.explanation: The cerebrum controls conscious sensation, interpretation and voluntary movement, so it is mainly responsible for deciding to press the brake after seeing the red light. The cerebellum coordinates balance, the medulla controls autonomic functions, and the hypothalamus regulates temperature and water balance.

questions.q: During a sudden fright on a bus in Onitsha, a passenger's pupils widen and heart rate increases. Which hormone most directly produces these rapid responses?
questions.explanation: Adrenaline from the adrenal medulla produces rapid fight-or-flight responses such as widened pupils and a faster heart rate. Thyroxine can raise metabolic rate over a longer period but does not produce such immediate effects.

questions.q: A woman in Ibadan has regular menstrual cycles. Which change in cervical mucus near ovulation most helps sperm survive and swim through the cervix?
options: It becomes thin, watery and more alkaline.
It dries up and forms a solid plug.
questions.explanation: Near ovulation, the cervical mucus becomes less thick, more watery and more alkaline, which helps sperm survive and swim through the cervix. Thick sticky or strongly acidic mucus makes sperm movement and survival more difficult.

questions.q: A man in Sokoto has a vasectomy. Which function is directly prevented by the operation?
options: Production of sperm cells in the testes stops immediately.
Testosterone secretion by the testes stops.
Urine flow from the bladder is blocked.
Sperm cells are prevented from passing from the testes to the urethra.
questions.explanation: Vasectomy blocks or cuts the vas deferens, so sperm cannot travel from the testes to the urethra for ejaculation. Sperm production and testosterone secretion by the testes continue, and urine flow is unaffected.

questions.q: A biology student in Ibadan examines a disease-causing agent obtained from a patient. It has no cellular structure, contains either DNA or RNA enclosed in a protein coat, and can multiply only inside living cells. The agent is best classified as a
questions.explanation: The lack of cellular structure, presence of a protein coat around nucleic acid, and inability to reproduce outside a living cell are characteristic of a virus. Bacteria are cellular and can reproduce outside host cells, while protozoans and fungi are cellular eukaryotic organisms.

questions.q: A student in Jos collects a flowering plant with a tap root system, net-veined leaves and floral parts in fives. The plant is best classified as a
questions.explanation: A tap root system, net venation and floral parts usually in fours or fives are features of dicotyledonous angiosperms. Monocots typically have fibrous roots and parallel venation, gymnosperms do not have true flowers, and pteridophytes do not produce seeds.

questions.q: An animal collected near a village in Bauchi has dry scaly skin, lays eggs with leathery shells on land, and breathes with lungs throughout life. It is classified as a
questions.explanation: Dry scaly skin, pulmonary respiration and shelled eggs laid on land are typical features of reptiles. Amphibians usually have moist skin and an aquatic larval stage, birds have feathers, and mammals have hair and mammary glands.

questions.q: In humans, the ability to roll the tongue is controlled by a dominant allele T, while inability to roll the tongue is recessive t. A man in Ilorin who cannot roll his tongue marries a woman who is heterozygous for tongue rolling. What is the probability that their first child will be unable to roll the tongue?
questions.explanation: The man is tt and the woman is Tt. Their possible offspring are Tt and tt in a 1:1 ratio, so the probability of a child being unable to roll the tongue (tt) is 1/2.

questions.q: A farmer in Zaria observes that maize plants growing near a river bank are taller and greener than those planted on a dry upland plot on the same day with the same seed. The most likely ecological factor responsible is
questions.explanation: The river-bank plot is likely to have more soil moisture, which supports photosynthesis and nutrient absorption, leading to taller and greener maize. Since the seed and planting date are the same, the difference is most likely due to water availability rather than the other factors listed.

questions.q: A student in Ibadan tests a soil sample from a rice field and finds a bacterium that converts ammonia to nitrite. The bacterium is most likely
questions.explanation: Nitrosomonas oxidises ammonia to nitrite during nitrification in the nitrogen cycle. Rhizobium fixes atmospheric nitrogen in root nodules, Nitrobacter converts nitrite to nitrate, and Pseudomonas includes denitrifying bacteria.

questions.q: A lichen growing on a rock in Jos is made up of an alga and a fungus living together. The alga supplies food by photosynthesis while the fungus provides shelter and minerals. This relationship is best described as
questions.explanation: In a lichen, both the alga and the fungus benefit, making the relationship mutualistic. Parasitism involves one organism benefiting and the other being harmed, while commensalism involves one benefiting and the other being unaffected.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes glycolysis in a cell?
options: It requires oxygen and directly produces most of the ATP made during aerobic respiration.
It occurs in the mitochondrial matrix and produces carbon dioxide and water.
It converts one glucose molecule into two pyruvate molecules in the cytoplasm without requiring oxygen.
It converts pyruvate into lactate in the cytoplasm when oxygen is available.
questions.explanation: Glycolysis takes place in the cytoplasm and breaks one glucose molecule into two pyruvate molecules without requiring oxygen. The mitochondrial reactions produce carbon dioxide and water, and most ATP in aerobic respiration is made later in the mitochondria, not during glycolysis.

questions.q: A student in Calabar observes numerous mitochondria in the middle piece of a human sperm cell. The main function of these mitochondria is to
options: secrete digestive enzymes to break down the egg membrane
produce the flagellum used for movement
release energy from glucose for the swimming movement of the sperm
questions.explanation: Mitochondria carry out aerobic respiration and release energy as ATP, which powers the movement of the sperm flagellum. Genetic information is stored mainly in the nucleus, digestive enzymes are associated with the acrosome, and the flagellum is not produced by mitochondria.

questions.q: During haemodialysis of a patient with kidney failure in Kano, the dialysis fluid contains glucose at the same concentration as normal blood plasma. What is the main reason for including glucose in the dialysis fluid?
options: to remove urea from the blood more quickly
to draw excess water out of the blood by osmosis
to supply the patient with extra glucose during the procedure
to prevent glucose from being lost from the patient's blood by diffusion
questions.explanation: The dialysis fluid has the same glucose concentration as normal plasma, so there is no net diffusion of glucose out of the blood. If the fluid contained no glucose, glucose would diffuse from the blood into the dialysate. Urea is removed because its concentration in the dialysis fluid is kept low.

questions.q: Which product of the breakdown of haemoglobin is excreted from the body in bile?
questions.explanation: When old red blood cells are broken down, the haem part of haemoglobin is converted into bile pigments such as bilirubin, which are excreted in bile. Urea comes mainly from deamination of amino acids, not from haemoglobin breakdown.

questions.q: A student in Lagos observes a cell under a light microscope and wants to decide whether it is eukaryotic. Which feature would confirm that it is eukaryotic?
options: a nucleus enclosed by a nuclear membrane
questions.explanation: Eukaryotic cells have a nucleus enclosed by a nuclear membrane, which is absent in prokaryotic cells. Cell walls, ribosomes and cytoplasm can occur in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells, so they do not confirm eukaryotic status.

questions.q: A potato tuber from Jos is found to contain many starch-storing plastids. Which type of plastid are they?
questions.explanation: Amyloplasts are starch-storing plastids found in cells such as potato tuber cells. Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll for photosynthesis, while chromoplasts contain pigments other than chlorophyll.

questions.q: At which joint is movement possible in all planes, including rotation?
options: joint between the atlas and axis
questions.explanation: The shoulder is a ball-and-socket joint, so it allows movement in several planes as well as rotation. Elbow and knee joints are hinge joints, and the atlas-axis joint is a pivot joint that mainly allows rotation.

questions.q: The bones that make up the human skull are held together by which type of joint?
questions.explanation: The bones of the skull are joined by fibrous sutures, which are immovable joints that protect the brain. Hinge, ball-and-socket and pivot joints are movable and occur elsewhere in the body.

questions.q: Glucose is absorbed from the ileum into the blood even when the glucose concentration in the intestinal lumen is lower than that inside the epithelial cells. Which process is mainly responsible?
questions.explanation: Glucose can be absorbed against its concentration gradient by active transport, which uses energy from ATP. Simple diffusion would only move glucose down its concentration gradient.

questions.q: Which change would increase the rate at which carbon dioxide diffuses from a respiring muscle cell into the blood?
options: a reduction in the concentration difference of carbon dioxide between the cell and the blood
a steeper concentration gradient of carbon dioxide between the cell and the blood
a decrease in the surface area of the capillaries
an increase in the thickness of the capillary wall
questions.explanation: Diffusion is faster when the concentration gradient is steeper, because more molecules move from the region of higher concentration to the region of lower concentration per unit time. Increasing the capillary wall thickness or reducing the capillary surface area would slow diffusion.

questions.q: The wings of a bat and the wings of a housefly perform the same function but differ in basic structure and origin. Such structures are described as
questions.explanation: Structures that carry out the same function but have different basic structure and origin are analogous. Homologous structures share a common basic plan even when their functions differ.

questions.q: In a population of insects on a farm in Ogun State, a few individuals carry a gene that makes them break down a pesticide. After repeated spraying, many insects in the population can break down the pesticide. Which statement best explains the change?
options: The pesticide caused all exposed insects to develop resistance and pass it to their offspring.
The insects learned to break down the pesticide after repeated exposure.
The resistant insects survived and reproduced, so the resistance allele became more common.
The resistance allele spread because the pesticide made the insects stronger.
questions.explanation: Repeated spraying selects insects that already carry the resistance allele; these survive, reproduce and pass the allele to their offspring. The change is therefore due to natural selection, not to the insects learning or to the pesticide creating resistance on demand.

questions.q: A tomato farmer in Jos notices dark, sunken patches at the bottom of several tomato fruits. Which mineral deficiency is most likely responsible?
questions.explanation: Dark, sunken patches at the blossom end of tomato fruits are typical of calcium deficiency. Calcium is needed for strong cell walls, and its shortage causes the fruit tissue to collapse.

questions.q: A student in Calabar investigates digestion and finds an enzyme in the small intestine that acts on maltose. Which enzyme breaks maltose into glucose molecules?
questions.explanation: Maltase hydrolyses maltose into two glucose molecules. Amylase acts mainly on starch, lipase on fats and pepsin on proteins.

questions.q: A child in Enugu with kwashiorkor has a swollen abdomen. Which explanation best accounts for this swelling?
options: Undigested starch ferments and produces gas that bloats the abdomen.
More protein than normal is digested, drawing water into the abdomen.
Low plasma protein reduces the osmotic pull of the blood, so fluid collects in body tissues.
Excess fat is stored in the abdomen because protein is unavailable.
questions.explanation: In kwashiorkor, low plasma protein lowers the osmotic pull of blood, so fluid moves into tissues and causes swelling. The swelling is not caused by gas from undigested starch or by extra fat storage.

questions.q: During a hot afternoon, a potted orange seedling in Ibadan loses water rapidly through its leaves. Which process mainly accounts for the upward movement of water in the xylem?
questions.explanation: Transpiration at the leaves creates a tension in the xylem that pulls water upward; cohesion between water molecules helps transmit the pull. Root pressure and capillary action contribute but are too weak to account for most upward movement in a tall plant.

questions.q: Mr Danjuma in Kaduna has a blockage in a coronary artery, reducing blood flow to the heart muscle. Which substance supply to the heart muscle is most immediately reduced?
questions.explanation: Coronary arteries supply the heart muscle with oxygen and glucose for aerobic respiration. If they are blocked, the muscle quickly lacks oxygen and energy, which can damage it.

questions.q: A patient in Kano with tuberculosis is advised to complete a six-month course of drugs even after feeling better. Why is this important?
options: To destroy remaining bacteria and reduce the chance of resistant strains developing.
To kill all normal bacteria in the digestive tract.
To make the BCG vaccine work in his body.
To prevent the drugs from causing an allergic reaction.
questions.explanation: Completing the course kills surviving bacteria that could cause a relapse. It also reduces the chance that partly eliminated bacteria develop resistance to the drugs.

questions.q: While washing plates in Akure, Bisi accidentally touches a hot pot. The impulse that travels from the skin receptors to the spinal cord is carried by which neurone?
questions.explanation: A sensory neurone carries impulses from a receptor such as pain receptors in the skin towards the central nervous system. A relay neurone links neurones within the spinal cord, while a motor neurone carries impulses away from the central nervous system to an effector.

questions.q: Musa in Osogbo suddenly meets a snake on a footpath. Which hormone is chiefly responsible for the rapid increase in his heart rate and the widening of his pupils?
questions.explanation: Adrenaline is released from the adrenal medulla during emergencies and prepares the body for action by increasing heart rate and widening the pupils. Insulin lowers blood glucose, thyroxine mainly regulates long-term metabolic rate, and antidiuretic hormone promotes water reabsorption in the kidneys.

questions.q: A health worker in Warri explains to students that sperm are stored before ejaculation in which structure of the human male?
questions.explanation: Sperm mature and are stored in the epididymis before being transported through the vas deferens during ejaculation. The seminal vesicle and prostate gland add secretions to semen, while the seminiferous tubules are the sites where sperm are produced.

questions.q: A pregnant woman in Ilesha attends an antenatal clinic. Which function is performed mainly by the amniotic fluid surrounding the developing foetus?
options: Supplying oxygen directly to the foetus
Carrying nutrients from the mother to the foetus
Protecting the foetus from mechanical shock
questions.explanation: Amniotic fluid cushions the foetus against mechanical shock and helps maintain a stable environment. The placenta is the structure mainly responsible for supplying oxygen, carrying nutrients to the foetus and producing several pregnancy hormones.

questions.q: A plant collected in Ilorin has flowers, and its seeds are enclosed within fruits. The plant is classified as a/an
questions.explanation: Angiosperms are flowering plants whose seeds are enclosed within fruits. Gymnosperms produce seeds not enclosed in fruits, while pteridophytes and bryophytes do not produce seeds.

questions.q: A lizard found in Sokoto is placed in the class Reptilia. Which combination of features best supports this classification?
options: Moist skin with mucus and eggs laid in water
Body covered with hair and mammary glands present
Body covered with feathers and warm-blooded
Dry scaly skin and shelled eggs laid on land
questions.explanation: Reptiles typically have dry scaly skin and lay shelled eggs on land, which reduce water loss and protect the embryo. Moist skin with eggs laid in water is characteristic of amphibians, feathers are characteristic of birds, and hair with mammary glands is characteristic of mammals.

questions.q: Mrs Bello in Kaduna is a carrier of an autosomal recessive condition with genotype Cc. Her husband has the homozygous normal genotype CC. What is the probability that their next child will be a carrier?
questions.explanation: The mother produces C and c gametes in equal numbers, while the father produces only C gametes. The possible offspring are CC and Cc in equal proportions, so half are expected to be carriers.

questions.q: In cattle, the alleles for red coat (R) and white coat (W) show codominance. A roan bull, genotype RW, is crossed with a white cow, genotype WW. What fraction of the offspring is expected to be roan?
questions.explanation: The roan bull produces R and W gametes in equal numbers, while the white cow produces only W gametes. The offspring are RW and WW in equal proportions, so half are expected to have the roan phenotype.

questions.q: A normal human somatic cell has 46 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are present in a mature sperm cell from a man in Owerri?
questions.explanation: A mature sperm cell is a gamete and is haploid, containing half the chromosome number of a somatic cell. Half of 46 is 23, comprising 22 autosomes plus either an X or a Y sex chromosome.

questions.q: A biology class in Jos studies a bare rock surface after a landslide. The first organisms to colonise the rock are usually
questions.explanation: Lichens are pioneer organisms that can survive on bare rock and help begin soil formation. Mosses, ferns and grasses normally become established later, after some soil and moisture have accumulated.

questions.q: In a pond near Epe, phytoplankton have a smaller total biomass than the fish that feed on them, yet the ecosystem remains stable. This is because phytoplankton
options: store more energy per gram than fish
contain more dry matter than fish
reproduce rapidly and are continually replaced as they are eaten
are not eaten by fish but only by decomposers
questions.explanation: An inverted pyramid of biomass can occur in aquatic ecosystems because phytoplankton multiply quickly and are constantly replaced, even though their standing biomass is small. They do not store more energy per gram than fish, nor are they ignored by fish.

questions.q: In a food chain, the energy available to snakes is much less than the energy available to frogs mainly because
options: living organisms lose much energy as heat during respiration at each trophic level
energy is converted entirely to biomass
decomposers return all energy to producers
energy is destroyed when animals eat one another
questions.explanation: At each trophic level, organisms use energy for respiration and release much of it as heat, so only a small fraction is passed on. Energy is not destroyed during feeding, and decomposers release matter and heat rather than returning all energy to producers.

questions.q: During normal inhalation by a student in Ilorin, which set of changes occurs?
options: The diaphragm contracts while the rib cage moves downward and inward.
The diaphragm relaxes while the rib cage moves upward and outward.
The diaphragm relaxes and becomes dome-shaped while the rib cage moves downward and inward.
The diaphragm contracts and flattens while the rib cage moves upward and outward.
questions.explanation: In inhalation, contraction of the diaphragm and external intercostal muscles increases the volume of the thorax and lowers the pressure inside, so air enters the lungs. Relaxation of the diaphragm and inward movement of the rib cage occur during exhalation.

questions.q: A patient in Ibadan with kidney failure is treated by dialysis. In the artificial kidney, urea leaves the blood mainly by
options: active transport into the dialysate against a concentration gradient
filtration under pressure from the dialysate into the blood
diffusion into the dialysate because its concentration is higher in the blood than in the dialysate
osmosis through a selectively permeable membrane into the blood
questions.explanation: Urea passes down its concentration gradient from the blood into the dialysate through a partially permeable membrane. Active transport is not the main method, and osmosis moves water rather than urea.

questions.q: Which substance is normally absent from the glomerular filtrate of a healthy person?
questions.explanation: Plasma proteins are too large to pass through the walls of the glomerular capillaries and the capsule in a healthy kidney. Glucose, urea and sodium ions are small enough to be filtered.

questions.q: Apart from water and salts, the main nitrogenous waste present in human sweat is
questions.explanation: Human sweat contains water, salts and a small amount of urea, so the skin helps excrete some nitrogenous waste. Ammonia is toxic and is mainly converted to urea in the liver, while uric acid is the main nitrogenous waste in birds and insects.

questions.q: A fresh cassava leaf cell is placed in distilled water. As water enters by osmosis, which structure expands most and presses the cytoplasm against the cell wall, making the cell turgid?
options: large central vacuole filled with cell sap
questions.explanation: Water accumulates in the large central vacuole, increasing turgor pressure and pressing the cytoplasm against the cell wall. The cell wall is strong and resists expansion rather than expanding most.
